@graph.name: If I can’t find tarragon, what other herbs work?

acceptedAnswer.text: While I do think fresh tarragon makes this recipe extra tasty, you could also use fresh chervil, basil, or dill. In a pinch, you could use dried tarragon (use about 1 teaspoon), though I do think fresh herb options are best.

recipeIngredient: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper (to taste)

itemListElement.text: Cover the chicken with water. Place the chicken breasts in a wide pot or pan and cover by about an inch with cold water. Season the water with salt. Optionally, you can add aromatics of your choice. Read my poached chicken recipe for more details.
itemListElement.name: Add

itemListElement.text: Simmer the chicken. Turn the heat to medium until it reaches a gentle simmer. Then reduce the heat back to low and cover the pan. Let the chicken simmer for 8 to 12 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 160°F to 165°F. Remove the chicken and let it rest for a couple of minutes. Then chill in the fridge.
itemListElement.name: Poach

itemListElement.text: Dice the cooled chicken. Transfer the cooled chicken to a cutting board and dice it into ½-inch pieces. Add it to a large mixing bowl.
itemListElement.name: Dice

itemListElement.text: Mix together and chill. Add the grapes, celery, green onion, mayonnaise, mustard, almonds, parsley, tarragon, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper, then stir together, until well combined. Let it chill covered in the fridge until you're ready to serve.
itemListElement.name: Slice

itemListElement.text: Serve. Transfer the salad to a serving bowl and garnish with additional fresh herbs, if you'd like.
itemListElement.name: Mix

review.reviewBody:
If you have dried tarragon the ratio is about one teaspoon instead of one tablespoon fresh. Probably want to mix it with the mayo and mustard first and let it sit before you mix the rest. 

I've made similar veronique recipes (tarragon and green grapes) and found myself in the same situation and was able to substitute an equal amount of mint and parsley, half each, and that worked fairly well.

Absolutely the best chicken salad recipe I have made! Loved the little bites with hints of lemon and tarragon. It feels like a nice update to older recipes with the added crunch of the almonds, too. Thank you!
Absolutely the best chicken salad recipe I have made! Love the little bites with hints of lemon and tarragon.

I just made this for my daughter's first birthday party and I have never gotten so many compliments or requests for a recipe than this chicken salad!! My stepdad loved it so much he said I could sell this stuff! it's a little more prep work than I usually do for a chicken salad but truly worth the time and effort - absolutely delicious and will be adding to my recipe book for party rotations!

Forgot to share that I made this TWICE during our family vacation in June.   I used a rotisserie chicken to save time, and it was incredible.  Served with butter lettuce cups and croissants.  The family said it is my "signature" dish and must make every time we are together.  

Jessica
I made this recipe and the salad was delicious! I only wish I made more!
